# Unrated Restaurants

*Generated by `src/unrated.py` from the cleaned Kaggle data. Nothing is typed in.*

**Unrated restaurants: 2,148 of 9,551 (22.5%).** In the raw file they have aggregate rating 0 and rating text 'Not rated'. A 0 here means 'no rating yet', not a bad rating.

## How they are treated

| area | rule | evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Cleaning | Raw rating 0 with 'Not rated' is treated as missing (blank), not as a real 0; flag is_rated = 0. | 2,148 of 9,551 restaurants (22.5%) |
| KPIs: counts | Restaurant, city, delivery and booking counts include unrated restaurants. | Restaurants KPI = 9,551 |
| KPIs: average rating | Average rating uses rated restaurants only. | 3.44 (rated only); it would be a misleading 2.67 if the zeros were counted |
| KPIs: total votes | Total votes includes the few votes unrated restaurants have. | Unrated restaurants hold 1,869 votes in total (max 3 each) |
| MySQL | aggregate_rating is stored as NULL, so AVG() skips unrated rows; is_rated column; a CHECK constraint keeps popularity_class NULL exactly when is_rated = 0; query Q24 shows the unrated share by city. | sql/01_schema.sql, sql/03_analysis_queries.sql |
| Power BI | Measures 'Rated Restaurants' and 'Unrated %'; Avg Rating is blank for unrated rows; the rating distribution shows 'Not rated' as a separate grey bar. | dashboards/powerbi/dax_measures.md |
| Tableau | Rating fields stay empty for unrated restaurants, so averages use rated restaurants only. | dashboards/tableau/TABLEAU_GUIDE.md |
| Model training | Excluded: they have no popularity class (the target needs a rating and votes). | Training and test use 7,403 rated restaurants |
| Model predictions | The saved model uses no votes or rating, so it can still predict for unrated restaurants. These predictions cannot be checked (no actual class). | Predicted for 2,148: Low 1,925 (89.6%), Medium 174 (8.1%), High 49 (2.3%) |

## Saved-model predictions for unrated restaurants

The saved model predicts for all 2,148 unrated restaurants: Low 1,925 (89.6%), Medium 174 (8.1%), High 49 (2.3%). These predictions describe what similar rated restaurants achieved; they cannot be checked, because unrated restaurants have no actual popularity class. File: `outputs/unrated/unrated_predictions.csv`.
